output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, there is a statistically significant negative relationship between time preference (as measured by savings behavior) and BMI in Hispanic men. This suggests that individuals with higher time preference (i.e., those who are less likely to dissave or have stable savings) tend to have lower BMI. The relationship is statistically significant, with a coefficient of approximately -1.38 and a p-value of approximately 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁵.
